about: The first of the three prayers the priest says bowed over the altar, hands joined upon it, before he receives — and the only one of the three that asks for anything beyond himself: peace and unity for the Church. Its opening quotes John 14:27 word for word as far as pacem meam do vobis, words spoken at the Last Supper on the eve of the departure; the Gospel goes on non quomodo mundus dat, not as the world gives, and the prayer lets that clause go. At solemn Mass the kiss of peace follows immediately out of it. In Masses for the dead the peace is not given and this prayer is not said.

s01.narrative: The priest bows over the altar with his hands joined upon it, and says the three prayers that follow secretly.

s02.translation: O Lord Jesus Christ, who didst say to Thine Apostles:

s03.translation: Peace I leave you, my peace I give you:

s04.translation: look not upon my sins, but upon the faith of Thy Church;

s05.translation: and vouchsafe to give her peace and to gather her into one according to Thy will:

s06.translation: Who livest and reignest, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

s07.narrative: In Masses for the dead the peace is not given, and this prayer is left out.

w002.function: The vocative of Jesus is Jesu, one of the few Greek endings Latin kept unaltered; Whitaker's does not carry the name at all, so this parse rests on Collatinus and the edition.

w005.function: Perfect: a thing said once, at a known hour, and standing said ever since — which is why the prayer can hold Him to it.

w006.function: Dative: said to whom — to them, at the Last Supper table.

w009.function: Relínquo is what a man does with what he leaves behind at his going; the words were spoken on the eve of the Passion.

w012.function: The second time the word is said it is qualified: not peace of any kind, but His own — and the quotation stops just before the Gospel's not as the world gives.

w015.function: With the subjunctive “respícias” (w016) it makes a negative petition, as it does in the Lord's Prayer: do not look.

w016.function: Re- and spício: to look back at, to turn and take notice. The prayer asks Him to turn His face one way and not the other.

w018.function: Singular “my”, though the priest is about to ask for the whole Church: the sins are his own, the faith is not.

w020.function: Set against “peccáta” (w017) as the thing to be looked at instead; the two accusatives are the two objects offered to the same verb.

w023.function: Two feminine nouns stand within reach — the faith and the Church — and the form settles neither. The two things asked, peace and gathering into one, are asked of the Church, and that is how the prayer is read.

w027.function: One of two infinitives depending on “dignéris” (w030); a verb made from pax, to make peaceful.

w029.function: Co- and adunáre, to bring to one: not to reconcile parties but to make many into one thing.

w030.function: Deponent — passive in form, active in meaning. The construction is the courtly one of the Roman prayers: not “do this” but “think it worthy to do this”.

w035.function: Nominative standing with the two verbs, not an address: who as God livest and reignest.
